slides.headline: Ring Cameras Leave Their Mounts
slides.subheadline: Amazon pairs a flying indoor camera with a wheeled business patrol robot.
slides.svgBlueprint: Use Paper #0D0E12, Ink #F1F3F9, Accent #FF4D00 and Surface #161820 throughout. Branch an orange trajectory upward toward an abstract drone glyph and horizontally toward a wheeled robot glyph. Place one product callout at each endpoint. Keep the headline above both paths. Glyphs are conceptual, not dimensionally accurate product renderings.

items.title: Ring Drone Cam
items.body: Flying indoor security camera.

items.title: Ring Rover Cam
items.body: Wheeled autonomous security robot designed for business.

slides.headline: Flight And Wheels, Different Prices
slides.subheadline: Drone targets home monitoring; Rover is designed for business.
slides.svgBlueprint: Draw two full-width ledger bands separated by an orange rule. Align product names left and oversized numerical price badges right. Add a small flight-path glyph to Drone and a wheel-track glyph to Rover. Use equal band heights; do not imply subscription costs are included.

slides.headline: Rover Ships First. Drone Awaits Authorization.
slides.subheadline: Rover has a scheduled shipping date; Drone’s target requires FCC authorization.
slides.svgBlueprint: Create a chronological horizontal track with two labeled milestones. Place Rover first using a solid marker. Place Drone second beyond an outlined FCC gate, connected by a dashed segment. Render full dates as editorial text, not numerical telemetry. Spacing is schematic, not a duration scale.

items.title: Ring Rover Cam
items.body: Preorders available; shipping scheduled to start December 16, 2026.

items.title: Ring Drone Cam
items.body: Target: January 27, 2027, conditional on Federal Communications Commission authorization.

slides.headline: An Eight-Minute Flight, Under Controlled Conditions
slides.subheadline: Flight time assumes a new, fully-charged battery under controlled conditions.
slides.svgBlueprint: Center an abstract drone glyph inside a circular rotation arrow. Add a field-of-view wedge corresponding to the stated angle. Position three numerical badges around the diagram with separate unit labels. Reserve an unobstructed text strip for the battery qualification. Do not depict coverage distance or flight range.

metrics.label: Minutes of flight time
metrics.context: New, fully-charged battery under controlled conditions.

slides.headline: Two Different Ways To Map Indoors
slides.subheadline: Both devices build digital floor plans, but their setup workflows differ.
slides.svgBlueprint: Draw one abstract, unmeasured floor-plan outline. Overlay a dashed hand-carried Drone route and a solid autonomous Rover route, differentiated by line pattern and endpoint glyphs. Place one annotation above and one below the shared plan. Mark the diagram as schematic; imply neither room count nor floor-transition capability.

items.title: Drone: customer-carried mapping
items.body: The customer carries the drone through indoor spaces to support mapping.

items.title: Rover: autonomous exploration
items.body: Autonomous exploration supports digital floor-plan mapping and suggested patrol points.

slides.headline: Autonomous Does Not Mean Local-Only
slides.subheadline: AI Pilot combines device cameras, specialized vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing.
slides.svgBlueprint: Build a vertical orange spine joining three compact annotations: shared AI Pilot processing, Drone subscription access, and Drone alert response. Use camera, cloud and route glyphs without additional text nodes. Keep processing arrows schematic; do not imply continuous uploading, processing location for every model, or a Rover subscription requirement.

items.title: Shared AI Pilot
items.body: Cloud processing works alongside device cameras, specialized vision models and on-device sensors.

items.title: Drone routes and schedules
items.body: Described for Amazon Ring Protect subscribers; subscription pricing is not stated.

items.title: Drone alert response
items.body: Ring camera, sensor or alarm notifications can trigger automatic set-route flights.

slides.headline: Ordinary Surfaces Can Complicate Navigation
slides.subheadline: Amazon identifies indoor surfaces around which Drone navigation performance may degrade.
slides.svgBlueprint: Draw a continuous schematic room section divided into three material zones: reflective flooring, a featureless matte wall, and glass or mirror panels. Use orange broken route segments near each zone to indicate possible navigation degradation, not inevitable crashes. Place one short annotation beneath each zone.

items.title: Reflective flooring
items.body: Polished marble or wet tile may degrade navigation performance.

items.title: Featureless walls
items.body: Blank matte walls without features may degrade navigation performance.

items.title: Glass and mirrors
items.body: Frameless glass and mirrors may degrade navigation performance.

slides.headline: Business Coverage, Bounded By The Floor
slides.subheadline: Rover’s coverage claim comes with single-floor and terrain restrictions.
slides.svgBlueprint: Use a large unmeasured floorplate with a Rover route and a prominent coverage annotation. Beneath it, place two restriction annotations: single-floor operation and incompatible terrain. Show a crossed stair glyph and an enlarged threshold detail labeled with the exact stated limit. Do not invent building dimensions or mast height.

items.title: Claimed coverage
items.body: Up to 5,000 square feet (465 square meters).

items.title: Operating environment
items.body: Single-floor, indoor environment; cannot climb stairs.

items.title: Incompatible terrain
items.body: Curved edges, sunken areas, black glossy floors; transitions greater than 1.375 inches (3.5 centimeters).

slides.headline: Encryption Claims Meet A Security Record
slides.subheadline: Amazon says Throw Away the Key Encryption will protect both new devices’ videos.
slides.svgBlueprint: Create three full-width evidence rows with distinct cloud, historical-account and encryption glyphs. Give each row equal visual weight. Separate historical FTC reporting from current product claims with explicit headings. Avoid shield checkmarks or imagery suggesting confirmed end-to-end encryption. Keep the full retention scope visible.

items.title: Rover cloud retention
items.body: Doorbell-ring, motion-event and Live View videos: cloud storage up to 180 days.

items.title: 2023 FTC investigation
items.body: The FTC described hackers accessing 55,000 US customers’ accounts.

items.title: EFF’s encryption assessment
items.body: Throw Away the Key Encryption remains well short of end-to-end encryption.
